summary: I spent eight years building real-time, data-driven software that millions of people use: live mobile games at Ubisoft's Kolibri Games, commercial PC titles on Steam, and VR training simulators used by the Bangladesh Army and Navy. I led teams of up to 12 and set up studios' engineering from zero.

Since 2026 I apply that engineering to AI. I work as the Forward Deployed AI Engineer at Dhaka Kacchi, a Berlin cloud kitchen, where I build and run its AI systems in production: an autonomous multi-agent marketing department, seven weekly-retrained ML models, a market-intelligence data platform, and live ML services anyone can try.
What I care about is the whole problem — understanding what a business actually needs, designing the right system, integrating it with what exists, deploying it, and measuring whether it worked.

loop.text: Sit with the people who own the problem. Turn it into a measurable target.
Find, collect and clean the data — often the hardest part.
Pick the simplest thing that works: rules, optimisation, classic ML, or agents.
Contracts, tests, CI, ADRs. AI systems are software systems.
Ship it behind real users, with guardrails and a human in the loop.
Measure cost and quality together, then iterate.
